title: I let AI analyze my last 100 trades and it humbled me...
author: Kasraborhan
selftext:
I've been trading for around six years, and one thing I've learned is that being profitable doesn't automatically mean you're trading well. You can finish a month green while making a bunch of mistakes that eventually catch up with you.

I wanted to see how useful AI actually is for reviewing trades, so I asked Zella AI to analyze my recent trading history, show me what I was doing well, and point out where I needed to improve.

It returned a breakdown in under a minute. The date-based report covered 98 trade sample.

**Here's what my dashboard showed:**

* Net P&L: +$6,127
* Win rate: 43.3%
* Profit factor: 1.24
* Average winner: $645
* Average loser: $396
* Win/loss ratio: 1.63

Profitable overall, but definitely plenty of room for improvement.

**The part that surprised me was my long vs. short performance.**

According to the AI breakdown, I took 84 longs that produced just $253 in profit, while 30 shorts generated $5,873.

I actually had a higher win rate on longs, too.

Now, that doesn't mean I'm suddenly going to become a short only trader. A few larger winners contributed heavily to those short results, and the sample isn't enough to prove one direction is better. (I will never be a long only or short only trader)

But it did make me question how selective I've been with my long setups. If I'm taking almost three times as many longs and barely making anything from them, that's worth investigating.

**Another thing it caught was my risk management.**

My average loser was around $396, but my biggest loss was $1,735. That's over four times my average loss.

I can sit here and say I understand risk management all day, but numbers like that are a reminder that knowing your rules and actually following them are two different things.

The AI also highlighted something I've struggled with for years: taking trades that are decent enough to justify an entry, but not necessarily good enough to deserve my risk and I took a LOT ofd these back in the day lol. Trading just to trade lol.

I trade mostly liquidity based setups, and sometimes I'll see part of my confirmation and convince myself the rest will follow. Occasionally it works, but those unnecessary attempts add up.

**So in the 3rd pic I shared what I want to do for the next 20 trades.**

One thing I want to make clear is that AI isn't some magical trading coach. Some of the aggregate numbers it returned didn't reconcile perfectly, so I still need to verify those against my journal.

But I did find it useful for quickly organizing months of trading history and giving me a few specific areas to investigate.

**For those of you who journal your trades, what's one statistic that completely changed the way you trade?**

I'm curious whether most people focus on win rate and P&L or actually dig into things like performance by direction, time of day, and setup quality.

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body: 100 trades is enough to spot a habit, not to prove one. the useful step is turning it into a rule you can check, like no new trade after two losses in a day. that check was the whole point when I built Quantradin: one rule replayed over years of past bars with fake money, free. quantradin.com. which habit did it flag first?

comments.author: FinnPowa___com
comments.body: I let AI analyse all my trades before buying. I user FinnPowa and so far so good. There no way you can analyse all the information required as well and as efficiently as AI, so I utilised the power of AI

replies.author: Kasraborhan
replies.body: There's so much data sitting in our trading history that most of us never properly analyze.

comments.author: Mikejiggidy
comments.body: Win rate and win loss ratio are not important metrics. Expectancy and profit factor is.

replies.author: Kasraborhan
replies.body: I agree that expectancy and profit factor give you a much better picture of whether you're actually making money, but I wouldn't say win rate and average win/loss are unimportant. They're literally part of what determines your expectancy 😂

replies.author: Mikejiggidy
replies.body: Your win rate can be 33% yet very profitable. Also, you can have a 70% win rate yet account balance dwindle.

comments.author: k1_r1
comments.body: the long side is what i'd dig into first. 84 longs for $253 is basically breakeven after all that effort, and since you already suspect the "half my confirmation showed up" entries, you could tag those separately and see if they're the ones dragging it down. the $1,735 loss is worth its own look too, one trade at 4x your average loser usually means a stop got moved. i work on portfoliolab and we have free paper accounts and backtesting, which is handy for testing a stricter long filter before it costs you anything

comments.author: pcsurv1vr
comments.body:
Interesting.  I won’t let AI trade for me but I used Excel’s built in AI to evaluate my trades and I agree it was eye opening.    Someone mentioned win rate as not being very important and I would agree with that up to a point.    I was able to see why trading strategies have worked this year and this quarter I have been focusing on the winning trade strategies.

As for win rate, I had a 100% win rate for September until I got stupid and did a day trade which blew up in a 15 second run of madness at the end of the 0DTE which corresponded to the last trading day of the Quarter, and cut the profit for the month from 95% to 35%. I do spreads, mainly SPX based on previous analysis.   So yes I agree that you can definitively learn (sometimes) and it has taught me what not to do.  There is however no excuse for stupid which creeps in from time to time.   (I’m not a day trader and I have no idea why I keep getting suckered into doing them about once per quarter).

Nice post OP.
